<explanation>
Below is a step-by-step guide for drawing an accurate, detailed architecture diagram for JavSP. Tailor each section to the project’s actual structure and purpose as revealed by the file tree and README:

1. Identify Project Type and Purpose
   • Type: A command-line, full-pipeline metadata scraper & organizer (no WebUI).  
   • Purpose:  
     – Parse video file names for AV identifiers.  
     – Crawl multiple external AV metadata websites in parallel.  
     – Aggregate, normalize, translate, and crop cover images.  
     – Generate NFO metadata files & organize folders for media servers (Emby/Jellyfin/Kodi).  
     – Auto-update itself, configurable via YAML or CLI flags.

2. Analyze the File Structure
   • Top-level “javsp” package: core modules.  
   • Subpackages:  
     – web/… – one crawler module per site (e.g. javbus.py, fanza.py).  
     – cropper/… – image-cropping interfaces & implementations (slimeface, utils).  
   • Core modules:  
     – __main__.py (CLI entry)  
     – config.py (loads config.yml)  
     – file.py (filename parsing & file‐ops)  
     – datatype.py, nfo.py (data models & NFO generation)  
     – lib.py, func.py (orchestration, threading, aggregation)  
     – image.py (cover downloading)  
     – prompt.py/translate.py (AI vs translation)  
     – print.py (console feedback)  
   • Support directories: data/ (static lookup), tools/ (migration & helpers), unittest/ (test harness).  
   • Deployment: Docker/Dockerfile, GitHub Actions workflows.

3. Examine README Insights
   • Multithreaded crawling, daily tests (CI).  
   • Uses AI-based cropping, translation service hooks.  
   • YAML-based configuration + CLI override.  
   • No persistent database; file system and JSON/NFO outputs.

4. Main Components & Interactions
   Draw boxes for each component, label clearly, and connect with arrows denoting data flow:

   a. CLI Layer  
      • Entry: javsp/__main__.py  
      • Responsibilities: parse CLI args, load config, invoke orchestration.  

   b. Configuration Module  
      • config.py reads config.yml / envrc / CLI flags.  
      • Supplies settings to all modules.  

   c. Filename Parser & File Manager  
      • file.py extracts AV codes, handles file system scanning, folder creation.  

   d. Crawler Manager (Orchestrator)  
      • func.py / lib.py create thread pool.  
      • Distributes AV codes to multiple WebCrawler workers.  

   e. WebCrawler Workers  
      • javsp/web/*.py – one class per site implements HTTP requests, parsing, exception handling.  
      • Connect to external web APIs/pages.  
      • Return normalized metadata objects.  

   f. Data Aggregation & Normalization  
      • datatype.py defines models (Title, Cast, Genres, etc.).  
      • lib.py merges data from multiple sources, resolves conflicts.  

   g. Translation Service  
      • prompt.py + web/translate.py call external translation API if enabled.  

   h. Image Downloader & Cropper  
      • image.py downloads high-res covers.  
      • cropper/interface.py selects correct algorithm.  
      • cropper/slimeface_crop.py applies AI cropping.  

   i. NFO Generator & File Writer  
      • nfo.py formats metadata into NFO/XML.  
      • print.py & file.py write NFO, artwork, organize directories.  

   j. Auxiliary Tools & Tests  
      • tools/* for config migration, version.  
      • unittest/* for unit and integration tests.  

   k. Deployment & CI  
      • Dockerfile → containerizes the entire app.  
      • GitHub Actions → runs unit tests, crawler tests, builds Docker image.

5. Highlight Architectural Patterns
   • Pipeline / Orchestration: sequential stages (parse → crawl → aggregate → transform → write).  
   • Strategy Pattern: one crawler per site, interchangeable.  
   • Factory Pattern: instantiate crawler based on site code.  
   • Thread Pool Concurrency: concurrent web requests.  
   • Plugin-like extensibility: adding new crawler modules under web/.  
   • Configuration-driven vs code-driven behavior.

6. Diagram Tailoring for a CLI/Ecosystem Tool
   • Emphasize the core pipeline above.  
   • Show no separate “frontend” box—CLI is entrypoint.  
   • Show extension points (web/ and cropper/ directories) as “plug-ins.”  
   • Represent config.yml as a distinct resource read at startup.  
   • Group all external HTTP services under one “External AV Sites” box, with arrows from each web/*.py.

7. Diagramming Guidelines
   • Use clear component labels (e.g., “Crawler Manager,” “Slimeface Cropper”).  
   • Directional arrows for data flow (→).  
   • Color-code:  
     – Blue for internal modules (core, orchestration).  
     – Green for external dependencies/services (websites, translation API).  
     – Yellow for I/O (config file, file system, Docker).  
   • Shapes:  
     – Rectangles for modules/services.  
     – Cylinders for data stores (static data/, output folders).  
     – Cloud icons for external sites/APIs.  
   • Annotate multithreading on the arrows between manager and worker modules.

8. Final Tips
   • Be exhaustive: include each top-level package and its role.  
   • Capture cross-cutting concerns: logging, error handling (exceptions.py), auto-update module.  
   • Keep layout logical: left-to-right data flow, top-to-bottom lifecycle.

By following this breakdown, your diagram will accurately reflect JavSP’s modular, plug-in crawler architecture, its file-based pipeline, and its integration points with external sites and AI services. Ensure every box, arrow, and label aligns with the actual Python modules and directories for maximum clarity.
